messages:
incident-bot: [PAGER] P0 - Avalanche (enterprise) reporting elevated 5xx + timeouts in eu-west-1. Affected: dedicated-pool-avalanche-eu. Paging on-call.

maria.sre: ack — I'm oncall, starting triage now. pulling logs / metrics.

maria.sre: quick findings: proxy returning 502/504s, backend runtime showing OOMs and several GPUs out of rotation. Autoscaler not keeping up. spikes on CPU & nvlink errors in logs.

sam.platform: looking at infra. If we need regional failover, plan is: warm capacity in eu-west-2 -> edge routing canary -> TTL drop & DNS cutover -> drain old pool.

jordan.oncall: taking DNS/drain lead. maria, does runtime use sticky sessions / KV cache that will break if we redirect at edge?

maria.sre: yes sticky cookie present (edge-sticky, TTL 300s). KV cache bindings will persist until clients reconnect. Recommend ramped redirect (canary -> 100%) + drop keepalives and set TCP close on proxy to reduce sticky tail.

priya.csm: customer impact: Avalanche reports ~40% errors for their API keys and several scheduled batch jobs failing. This is enterprise SLA. Preparing a customer-facing note for CS.

maria.sre: mitigation plan (v1):
1) Scale warm cluster in eu-west-2 to handle full pool (spin up 4 nodes).
2) Start 5% canary traffic to eu-west-2 via edge policy.
3) If canary healthy for 3m (no 5xx spike, latency OK), shift 100%.
4) Lower DNS TTL (300->60->10) and perform DNS cutover to reduce stragglers.
5) Drain & decommission affected nodes in eu-west-1 and triage GPU driver.

sam.platform: executing scale + health checks now. commands I'm running:
```
# scale warm pool
rctl infra scale --pool warm-eu-west-2 --count 4
# verify pool
rctl pool status dedicated-pool-avalanche-eu
```

maria.sre: initiating runtime drain guard for eu-west-1 backends (grace=120s):
```
./runtimectl drain --pool dedicated-pool-avalanche-eu --grace 120
```

ops-tilly: prepping DNS. current record TTL 300 -> setting 60 to speed cutover. will drop to 10 before final swap.
```
cloud-dns update --zone avalanche-prod --record api.avalanche.prod --ttl 60
```

jordan.oncall: canary at 5% live now. Monitoring:
- canary: 200 OKs, no 5xxs so far
- latency: stable (~120ms p95)
- metrics links: https://observability/redwood/alerts/avalanche (internal) :chart_with_upwards_trend:

maria.sre: noticed one backend in eu-west-1 crashed repeatedly with nvml driver errors — marking instance template and isolating. creating infra bug.

sam.platform: canary healthy for 4m. scaling edge route to 100% eu-west-2 now:
```
edgectl route set --service avalanche-api --weight eu-west-2=100
```

incident-bot: deploy-bot: edge policy change applied by sam.platform (commit abc123)

maria.sre: traffic switched to eu-west-2. immediate error rate dropped to baseline. starting full drain of eu-west-1 and kicking old connections.

priya.csm: customer comms: sent initial update — told customer we failed over to eu-west-2 and are monitoring. asked them to validate critical workflows. will post another update in 15m.

ops-tilly: dropping DNS TTL to 10 now. once propagation looks ok we'll remove old region endpoints from LB.
```
cloud-dns update --zone avalanche-prod --record api.avalanche.prod --ttl 10
```

jordan.oncall: seeing a small number of long-lived sessions still pinned to eu-west-1 (keepalives). I've killed the stale connections on the gateway and triggered token invalidation for sessions older than 5m.

maria.sre: post-action checks: all customer API keys in Avalanche back to 200s. latency stable. logging shows no new GPU errors in eu-west-2.

sam.platform: note for postmortem: autoscaler failed to react quickly because policy used average CPU over 5m window. Suggest adding a reactive short-window policy for enterprise dedicated pools and a pre-warmed buffer.

maria.sre: root cause (prelim): regression in GPU driver + autoscaler reaction window too long -> capacity exhaustion in eu-west-1 dedicated pool. Triggered 502s as proxy could not route to healthy runtime.

priya.csm: customer impact summary for comms: partial outage affecting ~47 minutes; customer transactional jobs retried; offering technical postmortem + SLA credits if applicable.

jordan.oncall: handing off follow-ups: infra to patch driver & bake template, platform to adjust autoscaler policies, SRE to add better warm-node alerts. I'll own post-incident checklist & coordinate with Priya for customer note.

maria.sre: creating follow-up tickets and adding action items. please link PM-7890 (postmortem) and INFRA-3124 (driver fix).

incident-bot: incident-severity:P1 -> transition to post-incident. Postmortem ticket created: PM-7890. :white_check_mark:

priya.csm: thanks team. I'll keep CS looped and file a summary for the customer success ledger.

jordan.oncall: taking it from here, tagging @sam.platform @maria.sre for triage sync tomorrow EOD. :thumbsup:
_meta: generated for dataset; single-thread slack transcript representing live incident coordination for an enterprise regional failover
